# Parameter perturbation of the augmented process {#sec-parameter-perturbation}

The contraction theorem is stated for each frozen parameter, with constants uniform on a specified region. We now compare two such frozen kernels, $Q_\theta$ and $Q_\vartheta$. The comparison is an operator calculation on Lipschitz test functions; it does not require constructing an additional coupling of the augmented transitions.

## One-step kernel regularity

For $f:\mathsf Z\to\mathbb{R}$ and $z=(x,u)$, write

$$
f_{\theta,u}(y)=f(y,T_\theta(y,u)).
$$ {#eq-pulled-back-test}

By @eq-augmented-kernel,

$$
Q_\theta f(x,u)=P_\theta f_{\theta,u}(x).
$$

Adding and subtracting $P_\vartheta f_{\theta,u}(x)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)f(x,u)
={}&(P_\theta-P_\vartheta)f_{\theta,u}(x)\\
&+P_\vartheta(f_{\theta,u}-f_{\vartheta,u})(x).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-augmented-operator-perturbation}

Under @asm-memory-lipschitz, $\|f_{\theta,u}\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_X)}\leq(1+L_T)\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}$, and

$$
|f_{\theta,u}(y)-f_{\vartheta,u}(y)|
\leq\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}
d_Y(T_\theta(y,u),T_\vartheta(y,u)).
$$

Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality therefore yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
&W_{d_Z}(Q_\theta((x,u),\cdot),Q_\vartheta((x,u),\cdot))\\
&\quad\leq (1+L_T)W_{d_X}(P_\theta(x,\cdot),P_\vartheta(x,\cdot))\\
&\qquad+P_\vartheta\!\left[
d_Y(T_\theta(\cdot,u),T_\vartheta(\cdot,u))
\right](x).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-one-step-parameter-bound}

The first term measures the change in the driving kernel; the second measures the change in the memory update under the same driving law. For the affine EMA, the second term depends only on $b_\theta-b_\vartheta$, since $A$ is fixed. In the square-root coordinates of @eq-sqrt-memory-update it can be controlled instead by the parameter difference of the original innovation $H_\theta$.

::: {#asm-parameter-kernel}
## Driver-level parameter regularity

On a parameter region $\mathsf K$, assume there is a measurable $w:\mathsf X\to[1,\infty)$ and constants $L_P,L_{T,\theta}<\infty$, uniform over $\theta,\vartheta\in\mathsf K$, such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_{d_X}(P_\theta(x,\cdot),P_\vartheta(x,\cdot))
&\leq L_P\|\theta-\vartheta\|w(x),\\
P_\vartheta[d_Y(T_\theta(\cdot,u),T_\vartheta(\cdot,u))](x)
&\leq L_{T,\theta}\|\theta-\vartheta\|w(x)
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-driver-parameter-assumptions}

for all $x$ and $u$ in the memory space under consideration. Let $\mathcal V:\mathsf Z\to[1,\infty)$ dominate $w(x)$ and suppose the family $(Q_\theta)_{\theta\in\mathsf K}$ has uniform geometric Wasserstein contraction as in @thm-wasserstein-lifting.
:::

The bounds in @asm-parameter-kernel are verification assumptions on the driver and forcing, not consequences of frozen contraction.

::: {#prp-augmented-kernel-regularity}
## One-step regularity of augmented kernels

Under @asm-memory-lipschitz and @asm-parameter-kernel,

$$
\gamma_{\theta,\vartheta}
:=\sup_{z\in\mathsf Z}
\frac{W_{d_Z}(Q_\theta(z,\cdot),Q_\vartheta(z,\cdot))}
{\mathcal V(z)}
\leq L_Q\|\theta-\vartheta\|,
$$ {#eq-augmented-perturbation-gamma}

with $L_Q=(1+L_T)L_P+L_{T,\theta}$. Equivalently, for every $d_Z$-Lipschitz test $f$,

$$
|(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)f(z)|
\leq L_Q\|\theta-\vartheta\|\mathcal V(z)
\|f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}(d_Z)}.
$$ {#eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound}
:::

::: {.proof}
Apply @eq-one-step-parameter-bound, substitute @eq-driver-parameter-assumptions and divide by $\mathcal V(z)\geq w(x)$. The equivalent operator estimate is the dual representation of $W_{d_Z}$.
:::

## Perturbation of invariant laws

The geometric estimate of @thm-wasserstein-lifting and the weighted one-step bound are the hypotheses appearing in the Wasserstein perturbation framework of [@RudolfSchweizer2018, Theorem 3.1]. The stationary specialisation can also be seen directly from the operator decomposition.

::: {#cor-invariant-parameter}
## Lipschitz dependence of augmented invariant laws

Assume @prp-augmented-kernel-regularity and suppose the invariant laws satisfy

$$
\sup_{\theta\in\mathsf K}\nu_\theta(\mathcal V)\leq M_{\mathcal V}<\infty.
$$ {#eq-uniform-invariant-moment}

Then for every $\theta,\vartheta\in\mathsf K$,

$$
W_{d_Z}(\nu_\theta,\nu_\vartheta)
\leq \frac{C_Z(\eta)L_QM_{\mathcal V}}{1-\eta}
\|\theta-\vartheta\|.
$$ {#eq-invariant-parameter-regularity}
:::

::: {.proof}
Fix a $1$-Lipschitz $f$. Since $\nu_\theta$ and $\nu_\vartheta$ are invariant,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\nu_\theta(f)-\nu_\vartheta(f)|
\leq{}&
|(\nu_\theta-\nu_\vartheta)(Q_\theta^n f)|\\
&+|\nu_\vartheta(Q_\theta^nf-Q_\vartheta^nf)|.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first term is at most $C_Z(\eta)\eta^n W_{d_Z}(\nu_\theta,\nu_\vartheta)$. For the second use

$$
Q_\theta^n-Q_\vartheta^n
=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}Q_\vartheta^j
(Q_\theta-Q_\vartheta)Q_\theta^{n-1-j}.
$$ {#eq-perturbation-telescope}

The stationarity of $\nu_\vartheta$, @eq-weighted-pointwise-operator-bound and the bound
$\|Q_\theta^k f\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\leq C_Z(\eta)\eta^k$
give

$$
|\nu_\vartheta(Q_\theta^nf-Q_\vartheta^nf)|
\leq C_Z(\eta)L_Q\|\theta-\vartheta\|\,
\nu_\vartheta(\mathcal V)\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\eta^{n-1-j}.
$$

Let $n\to\infty$. The first term tends to zero, and the geometric sum is bounded by $(1-\eta)^{-1}$. Taking the supremum over $f$ proves @eq-invariant-parameter-regularity.
:::

Uniform drift constants in @eq-augmented-drift, together with suitable moment conditions, provide one route to @eq-uniform-invariant-moment. The constant in @eq-invariant-parameter-regularity is not asserted to be uniform on parameter regions where the contraction, moment or perturbation constants diverge.

## Regularity of the stationary Adam field

Suppose $G_\theta:\mathsf Z\to\mathbb{R}^d$ has a uniform Lipschitz seminorm and satisfies

$$
\|G_\theta(z)-G_\vartheta(z)\|
\leq L_{G,\theta}\|\theta-\vartheta\|\mathcal V(z).
$$ {#eq-observable-parameter-assumption}

For $F(\theta)=\nu_\theta(G_\theta)$, add and subtract $\nu_\vartheta(G_\theta)$ to obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|F(\theta)-F(\vartheta)\|
\leq{}&
\|G_\theta\|_{\operatorname{Lip}}\,
W_{d_Z}(\nu_\theta,\nu_\vartheta)\\
&+\nu_\vartheta(\|G_\theta-G_\vartheta\|).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-field-parameter-bound}

Thus @cor-invariant-parameter gives local Lipschitz regularity of $F$ under @eq-observable-parameter-assumption. For the square-root memory coordinates of @eq-adam-lipschitz-readout the readout is independent of $\theta$, so the second term vanishes. This is a regularity conclusion for the *stationary* field, not yet an ODE approximation for the changing-parameter recursion.
